subject: Price-match request & packaging options for potential Nimbus migration
messages:
From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@nimbus.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: price match + packaging options for potential move

Hi Tessa,

We’re evaluating a migration from our current provider to Redwood and we have a competitive offer on the table. Before we proceed with an internal procurement recommendation, procurement asked me to check whether Redwood can match the commercial terms. High level:

- Current offer: vendor X is offering a 22% discount off list for the next 12 months, plus a $75k onboarding credit and 6 months of free pilot capacity.
- Our footprint: ~120M tokens / month (mostly generation), 12 training-adjacent inference nodes for fine-tuned models, bursty daytime traffic.
- Key asks: price parity (or better), a short pilot with credits for migration validation, and a clear SLA for 99.9% availability + rate guarantees.

Can you share what packaging you’d propose (consumption vs reserved), and whether there’s room to match the 22% + onboarding credit? We have a procurement deadline of Fri, Nov 19.

I’ve attached the competitor quote for reference.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Samuel Park
Head of Procurement, Nimbus AI
[attachment: competitor_quote.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: price match + packaging options for potential move

Hi Samuel — thanks for the details and for sharing the quote. We’d love to make this work. Quick notes up front:

- We can be competitive on the commercial band, but the best structure depends on how predictable your runtime needs are and whether you want to lock committed capacity (Redwood Dedicated) or stay consumption-first.
- Two packaging options that typically close for customers in your profile: 
  1) Consumption-focused: matched per-token rate with a 3-month $50k pilot credit and operational credits (onboarding hours) to subsidize migration. This preserves flexibility but has smaller up-front credit.
  2) Reserved/commit: 12-month reserved capacity with a steeper effective discount (we can approach 25% off list on equivalent MRR when combined with a one-time onboarding credit of $75k and a prioritized migration window). Also includes rollback protection if consumption diverges.

On SLA: we can include a 99.9% availability target in the SOW for Dedicated customers and a credit schedule for sustained breaches; for hosted customers we can map realistic latency SLAs by region.

Next steps I suggest:
- Quick 30-min call (tomorrow or Thu) to confirm expected monthly token mix and peak concurrency (so we can size reserved units vs consumption).
- If you prefer, I’ll put together an initial pricing grid showing both options and total cost-of-ownership over 12 months.

Attached is an initial pricing grid template I’ll use to model both options. If you can confirm a few usage numbers I’ll return a modeled comparison by EOD Thu.

Would Thu 11:00am PT work for a call?

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0184
[attachment: initial-pricing-grid.xlsx]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: price match + packaging options for potential move

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Nimbus’ ask. Short summary and proposed approach below: 

Summary:
- Prospect: Nimbus AI (large generative footprint ~120M tokens/mo).
- Competitor asks: 22% off + $75k onboarding credit + 6 months pilot. Procurement deadline Nov 19.

Proposed commercial options for approval: 
A) Consumption-first play: Match 22% on per-token list + $50k pilot credit (less than competitor but better operational support). Pros: preserves flexibility; lower opex risk. Cons: may lose to competitor’s higher credit.

B) Commit-heavy play: Offer 25% off list with a $75k onboarding credit if they sign a 12-month reserved commitment at an agreed baseline (commit covers ~80% of expected baseline consumption). Add clause: 1x 30-day migration support window + SLA with credit.

Risks: sets precedent for 25% on 12-months; bigger churn risk if they underconsume the commit. Recommend we accept B if we get a clear baseline and opt-out protection (true-up window + limited downgrade tolerance).

If you’re okay with B, I’ll thread legal for a SOW with migration credits and a limited rollback clause (we avoid open-ended credits).

— Tessa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: price match + packaging options for potential move

Tessa — I support option B with the caveats you raised. Two operational bullets I want in the SOW:
1) A defined true-up cadence (quarterly) and a modest overage rate for burst months so we’re protected if their consumption spikes.
2) Migration success metric: runbook acceptance + one staged production cutover window; onboarding credit tied to milestones not time.

Ask legal to include a limited first-year concession cap (so this deal doesn’t become a template). Once we have that, greenlight from me to move forward.

Jonas
Sales Director — Redwood Inference

From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@nimbus.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: price match + packaging options for potential move

Tessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for laying out both options. After internal review we prefer the reserved/commit option (your option B) provided we can get: 

- The 25% effective discount clarified in a line-item SOW.
- $75k onboarding credit applied to the first invoice and tied to migration milestones (runbook signoff + staged cutover).
- SLA language for 99.9% availability and a defined credit schedule.
- Quarterly true-up cadence (agree).

If you can send a redlined SOW and a DocuSign-ready agreement with these items, procurement will review and we should be able to get signatures before Nov 26. We also attached a short decision note for your records.

Samuel Park
Head of Procurement, Nimbus AI
[attachment: Nimbus-decision-note.pdf]
